jobs.title: Associate Director, Investment Data - SLC Management
jobs.description:
SLC Management is a growing global asset management firm providing innovative and diversified investment solutions to institutional investors. We are breaking new ground with a full spectrum of solutions for a growing institutional client base of more than 1400 organizations. Our history of organic and strategic growth reflects this commitment with over CA$422/US$304 billion in assets under management (AUM). As a subsidiary of Sun Life, we are aligned with one of the world’s leading financial services companies, and benefit from the stability and strength of that relationship.

We are a performance-driven organization with a deliberate focus on fostering a development-focused, inclusive culture revolving around our Core Values of being client obsessed
, valuing each other
, acting with speed
and having an owner’s mindset
. As part of our team, you play a role in fulfilling our purpose and making a difference. We offer a rewarding work environment that is filled with opportunity for growth where you will be empowered to meet the challenges of a highly competitive landscape.

Visit our website to learn more and for the most up to date AUM information.

SLC Management offers a mix of in-office and virtual work where our employees are empowered to do their best. Generally, employees are expected to work three or more days in-office each week with flexibility depending on their business, client and team needs.

Job Description:

Associate Director, Investment Management Data – SLC Management

What is in it for you:

Reporting to the Director, Investments Data Product, this role will be part of a dedicated Agile team and will be accountable for delivering investment data products through a highly dynamic and fast-paced solution development process.

The Associate Director will work closely with business stakeholders, data engineers, architects, and development teams to transform business concepts and data requirements into scalable solutions. This role is accountable for balancing business priorities, user needs, data quality requirements, governance objectives, and technology considerations while ensuring successful business outcomes.

The Associate Director will combine product ownership responsibilities with hands-on data analysis and domain expertise to define, develop, and continuously improve investment data products used across the organization.

What You Will Do

Contribute to the strategy, roadmap, and ongoing evolution of investment data products by translating business priorities into scalable solutions that improve decision-making, analytics, operational efficiency, and information management.
Partner with business and technology stakeholders to understand business processes, challenges, and data requirements, translating needs into user stories, acceptance criteria, data mappings, process documentation, and solution designs.
Perform data analysis, profiling, reconciliation, validation, and root-cause investigations across investment and accounting data domains, while collaborating with engineers and architects to design scalable data models, transformation rules, and reusable data products.
Own and prioritize the product backlog, ensuring delivery teams have clear requirements, priorities, and expected outcomes, while actively supporting Agile ceremonies, testing, user acceptance activities, and release readiness.
Support enterprise data governance, quality, and control initiatives by establishing and monitoring data standards, testing practices, lineage, metadata, and business glossary requirements.
Build strong relationships with stakeholders by communicating product priorities, roadmaps, progress, risks, and outcomes, while supporting change management and user adoption activities.
Contribute to the definition, tracking, and achievement of product and initiative objectives and key results (OKRs), measuring success through adoption, data quality, operational efficiency, and business outcomes.

What You Need To Succeed

6+ years of experience in Asset Management, Capital Markets, Investment Operations, Investment Technology, or a related field, with a strong understanding of investment products, portfolios, transactions, performance, benchmarks, market data, reference data, and investment lifecycle processes.
Demonstrated experience partnering with business stakeholders in data-intensive environments, including business analysis, requirements gathering, process improvement, data profiling, data mapping, testing, and solution delivery.
Strong knowledge of enterprise data management concepts, including data governance, data quality, data modeling, architecture, system integration, investment data platforms, and complex datasets, supported by advanced SQL and analytical skills.
Experience working as a Product Owner, Business Analyst, Data Analyst, or similar role within Agile delivery environments, with responsibility for backlog management, prioritization, user story development, and iterative solution delivery.
Proven ability to independently solve complex business and technology challenges, manage competing priorities, navigate ambiguity, influence stakeholders, and translate business needs into actionable solutions and measurable outcomes.
Experience with investment systems and enterprise data platforms is considered an asset.

Why SLC Management?

Opportunity to work for a growing global institutional asset manager
Excellent benefits and wellness programs to support the three pillars of your well-being – mental, physical and financial – including generous vacation and sick time, market-leading maternity, parental and adoption leave top up program, a partially-paid sabbatical program and much more
Pension, stock and savings programs with an employer-paid match to help build and enhance your future financial security
A flexible work environment with a friendly, caring, collaborative and inclusive culture focused on career growth development #WeWinAsATeam
The opportunity to move along a variety of career paths with amazing networking potential
Award winning workplace culture - Great Place to Work® Certified in Canada and the U.S., “Best Places to Work” by Glassdoor, Award for Excellence for Mental Health at Work, “Best Places to Work in Money Management” by Pension & Investments

SLC Management is a regulated business, and this means that there are certain financial reporting and trading preclearance requirements for all employees. Successful candidates will be required to declare personal investment accounts and securities investments as well as seek preclearance on future transactions including those of household members.

Job Category:

Business Analysis - Systems

Salary Range

85,000/85 000 - 128,000/128 000

We are committed to pay transparency and equity. The base salary range for this role is competitive and we strive to ensure that compensation is fair and equitable. Your actual base salary will be determined by your unique skills, qualifications, experience, education, and geographic location. In addition to base salary, this position is eligible for a discretionary annual incentive award based on individual and overall business performance along with a broad range of competitive benefits.

We are committed to fostering an inclusive environment where all employees feel they belong, are supported and empowered to thrive. We are dedicated to building teams with varied experiences, backgrounds perspectives and ideas that benefit our colleagues, clients, and the communities where we operate. We encourage applications from qualified individuals from all backgrounds.

We may use artificial intelligence to support candidate sourcing, screening, interview scheduling.

We will make reasonable accommodations to known physical or mental limitations. Persons with disabilities who need accommodation in the application process or those needing job postings in an alternative format may e-mail a request to thebrightside@sunlife.com.

We thank all applicants for showing an interest in this position. Only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

jobs.description:
Who are we?

Equinix is the world’s digital infrastructure company®, shortening the path to connectivity to enable the innovations that enrich our work, life and planet.

A place where bold ideas are welcomed, human connection is valued, and everyone has the opportunity to shape their future.

A career at Equinix means being at the center of shaping what comes next and amplifying customer value through innovation and impact. You’ll work across teams, influence key decisions, and help shape the path forward. You’ll find belonging, purpose, and a team that welcomes you—because when you feel valued, you’re empowered to do your best work.

Job Summary

The Vice President, Finance Transformation is a strategic executive leader responsible for driving the modernization and optimization of the Finance organization. This role leads a centralized team of transformation experts charged with designing and executing enterprise-wide finance initiatives that improve operating effectiveness, organizational scalability, processes, systems, data, and ways of working.

The Vice President, Finance Transformation serves as a key advisor to the Chief Financial Officer and Finance Leadership Team, translating strategic priorities into actionable transformation programs. This leader will oversee initiatives including organizational design, location and workforce strategy, shared services optimization, technology enablement, automation, artificial intelligence adoption, process excellence, governance, and change management to build a world-class Finance function.

Responsibilities

Finance Transformation Strategy

Develop and lead the multi-year Finance Transformation roadmap aligned to business and Finance objectives
Partner with the Chief Financial Officer and Finance Leadership Team to identify opportunities to improve efficiency, scalability, agility, and decision-making capabilities
Establish transformation priorities, business cases, milestones, and success metrics
Drive cross-functional alignment and executive sponsorship for major transformation initiatives

Organizational and Operating Model Excellence

Lead Finance organizational redesign efforts, including workforce planning, role optimization, and operating model evolution
Develop global location strategies, including shared services, centers of excellence, and hub-based delivery models, and oversee execution
Evaluate and implement organizational structures that improve efficiency and talent utilization
Ensure Finance capabilities are aligned with future business needs

Process Optimization and Continuous Improvement

Champion process standardization and simplification across all Finance functios
Implement best-in-class operating practices and continuous improvement methodologies
Identify opportunities to reduce complexity, improve controls, and enhance service delivery
Establish governance models that drive accountability and measurable outcomes

Technology and Digital Transformation

Partner with Finance Systems, Information Technology, and business stakeholders to develop and manage a multi-year roadmap to modernize Finance technology platforms
Oversee implementation and optimization of planning, reporting, consolidation, enterprise resource planning, automation, and analytics tools
Lead adoption of emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence, machine learning, data automation, and advanced analytics capabilities
Ensure Finance technology investments deliver measurable business value

Program Management and Change Leadership

Build and lead a high-performing transformation office responsible for delivering strategic initiatives
Establish rigorous program management disciplines, including prioritization, governance, risk management, and benefits tracking
Lead organization-wide change management efforts supporting transformation adoption
Foster a culture of innovation, accountability, and continuous improvement

Stakeholder Management

Serve as a trusted advisor to Finance executives and key business partners
Coordinate transformation efforts across Finance, Human Resources, Information Technology, Operations, and Corporate Functions
Provide regular updates to executive leadership regarding transformation progress, risks, and outcomes

Qualifications

Required Experience

Proven years of progressive experience in Finance, Consulting, Business Transformation, or Operational Excellence roles
Proven years leading large-scale transformation initiatives within complex organizations
Demonstrated success driving Finance operating model, process, and technology transformations
Experience leading enterprise programs involving multiple stakeholders and executive-level sponsors
Strong people leadership experience, including building and developing high-performing teams

Preferred Experience

Background in management consulting, corporate transformation, or finance strategy
Experience with enterprise resource planning, planning, and finance technology implementations
Experience developing global location and shared services strategies
MBA, CPA, CMA, or equivalent advanced business credential preferred

Competencies

Demonstrates strategic thinking and an enterprise mindset
Builds credibility as a trusted advisor and influences executive stakeholders effectively
Leads large-scale organizational change with clarity, discipline, and accountability
Collaborates effectively across functions, geographies, and levels of the organization
Establishes rigorous program governance and drives execution excellence
Uses data and measurable outcomes to inform decisions and track business value
Builds, develops, and inspires high-performing teams

jobs.title: VP, Strategic Finance Partner - Operations
jobs.description:
Who are we?

Equinix is the world’s digital infrastructure company®, shortening the path to connectivity to enable the innovations that enrich our work, life and planet.

A place where bold ideas are welcomed, human connection is valued, and everyone has the opportunity to shape their future.

A career at Equinix means being at the center of shaping what comes next and amplifying customer value through innovation and impact. You’ll work across teams, influence key decisions, and help shape the path forward. You’ll find belonging, purpose, and a team that welcomes you—because when you feel valued, you’re empowered to do your best work.

Job Summary

The Vice President, Strategic Finance Partner - Operations leader serves as the senior finance advisor to the Global Operations organization. The role shapes strategy, drives profitable growth, optimizes resource allocation, supports critical financial decisions, and leads global finance teams to maximize business performance and long-term value creation.

As a trusted member of the leadership team, the Vice President evaluates investments, assesses risks and trade-offs, and provides financial leadership on the business's most critical decisions. Partnering across the business, Controllership, Centers of Excellence, Finance Transformation, and other Global Finance functions, the role connects strategy to measurable outcomes, drives accountability, and enables informed decision-making.

Responsibilities

Strategic Business Partnership

Serve as the primary finance thought partner to executive leaders within the supported function, shaping strategic priorities, the growth agenda, and the choices that define where the business competes and invests.
Bring an independent, commercially grounded point of view to strategy discussions; challenge assumptions, surface blind spots, and influence executive decisions through insight rather than reporting.
Participate as a full member of the functional leadership team and contribute to the setting of business strategy, not only its financial translation

Strategic Decision-Making

Frame the most consequential decisions facing the function, define the options under consideration, and establish the criteria and trade-offs leadership will use to choose between them
Set the analytical agenda; determine which questions need answering and commission the required modeling and analysis from the Financial Planning and Analysis Center of Excellence
Translate analytical output into clear recommendations, and hold the line on decision quality, pace, and follow-through

Future-Focused Business Models and Scenarios

Define the design of forward-looking business and economic models used to evaluate new markets, pricing and commercial models, partnerships, and operating model shifts
Shape scenario and sensitivity frameworks around the strategic uncertainties that matter most, and use them to pressure-test the durability of the strategy.
Interpret long-range outlooks and competitive, market, and macro signals to anticipate inflection points before they show up in results

Input on Business Strategy

Co-own the functional strategy and long-range plan with business leadership, ensuring strategic choices are economically sound and value-creating
Advise on growth, portfolio, and capability-building choices, including build, buy, and partner options, and their implications for the operating model

Capital and Portfolio Choices

Guide where capital, talent, and management attention are deployed across competing strategic priorities
Challenge and endorse major business cases on strategic merit and expected value, rather than preparing them
Advocate for reallocation away from lower-value activity and advise on the structural economics of the function
Sponsor post-decision reviews so the organization learns from the bets it has placed

Partnership with the Center of Excellence

Partner with the Center of Excellence for planning cycles, forecasting production, model building, standard reporting, and data management; help define requirements and quality standards
Set priorities and service expectations with Center of Excellence leadership, and translate its output into executive-ready insight, narrative, and recommendations

Team Leadership

Lead a focused senior business partnering team built for judgment, influence, and strategic insight, shifting from transactional throughput to business outcome
Create a culture of curiosity, constructive challenge, speed, collaboration, and accountability for business outcomes
Develop finance talent capable of operating credibly with executives and building succession for partnering roles
Foster a strong operating rhythm across the business, Strategy, and the Center of Excellence

Qualifications

Required Experience

Proven years of progressive finance experience, with a clear track record in strategic finance and executive-level business partnering
Experience partnering with major business functions such as Global Operations, Product, Engineering, Information Technology, Marketing, Customer Success, or Corporate Functions
Proven record of influencing strategy and major investment decisions at the executive level
Strong command of value creation, long-range planning, scenario design, and business model economics
Experience operating in a model where planning, modeling, and reporting are delivered by a shared Financial Planning and Analysis Center of Excellence

Preferred Experience

Experience in large-scale, global, or high-growth organizations, ideally including business partnering, corporate strategy, and global leadership exposure
Demonstrated ability to influence executive decision-making without direct authority
Deep knowledge of the supported function's strategy, competitive dynamics, and value drivers
MBA, CPA, CFA, or equivalent advanced business credential preferred

Competencies

Demonstrates strategic thinking, a growth mindset, and sound business judgment
Influences executive stakeholders and communicates with clarity and impact.
Applies strong commercial and financial acumen to complex business decisions
Frames complex, ambiguous decisions and clarifies options and trade-offs
Prioritizes capital, talent, and resources against the highest-value opportunities
Constructively challenges leaders while balancing competing priorities
Collaborates effectively across functions, geographies, and levels of the organization
Builds, develops, and inspires high-performing global teams

jobs.title: Director, Sales Strategy & Resident Experience
jobs.description:
Mission

Job Description

As the Director, Sales Strategy & Resident Experience, you will contribute to Extendicare's purpose of Helping People Live Better by leading the regional sales function across a portfolio of retirement residences. Reporting to the Regional Director of Operations, you will provide direct leadership to residence-based sales professionals and work closely with Operations, Finance, and Marketing to maximize portfolio performance. This role is accountable for developing and executing Key Performance Indicators that achieve occupancy, rate, revenue, and NOI objectives. Through your strategic thinking, operational execution, and coaching, you will build a culture of accountability and results while ensuring an exceptional experience for prospects, residents, and families.

Key Outcomes

Achieve portfolio occupancy, revenue, market rate, and NOI targets through the development and execution of regional sales, education, occupancy, pricing, and revenue strategies.
Drive sustainable occupancy growth by increasing lead generation, conversion rates, and resident retention across the portfolio.
Optimize pricing and revenue performance by maintaining competitive market positioning, managing resident rate increases, and ensuring optimal inventory management and suite utilization.
Lead and develop a high-performing, accountable sales team that demonstrate Extendicare's Values and deliver results, including exceptional customer experience, and continuous quality improvement.
Ensure consistent, exceptional customer experience throughout the sales journey, including seamless transitions from prospect to resident.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Revenue & Occupancy Leadership
Lead the development and execution of regional sales, training, occupancy, pricing, and revenue strategies across a portfolio of retirement residences.
Accountable for achieving portfolio occupancy, revenue, market rate, and NOI targets.
Analyze market trends, competitor activity, customer demographics, and performance metrics to identify growth opportunities.
Develop and implement strategic initiatives that increase lead generation, conversion rates, occupancy growth, and resident retention.
Partner with Operations and Finance to establish annual revenue targets, budgets, and forecasts.
Pricing & Revenue Management
Maintain accountability for portfolio pricing strategies and rate management.
Review and approve annual and interim resident rate increases in accordance with company policy and market positioning.

jobs.title: Senior Director, Commercial & Regional Finance, AMER
jobs.description:
Who are we?

Equinix is the world’s digital infrastructure company®, shortening the path to connectivity to enable the innovations that enrich our work, life and planet.

A place where bold ideas are welcomed, human connection is valued, and everyone has the opportunity to shape their future.

A career at Equinix means being at the center of shaping what comes next and amplifying customer value through innovation and impact. You’ll work across teams, influence key decisions, and help shape the path forward. You’ll find belonging, purpose, and a team that welcomes you—because when you feel valued, you’re empowered to do your best work.

Job Summary

Equinix is seeking a highly skilled and experienced Senior Director of Commercial and Regional Finance. This leader is the key business partner to the Regional Presidents, Country Managing Directors, Corporate Development, and Business Development, sitting in-region and on the regional leadership team to drive cross-functional financial performance.

The role provides commercial support and finance business partnering for the Regional Presidents to enable better collaboration, communication, and outcomes. This position serves as the single finance point of contact for the Regional Presidents in navigating the finance organization, with a dotted-line reporting relationship to them.

The team aligns on metro strategy with regional leaders and partners with Sales, Revenue Operations, Capacity, Operations, and Corporate Development to maximize return on invested capital. The role also coordinates with finance peers on forecasting, budgeting, and reporting of regional profit and loss performance, as well as the Regional President’s selling, general, and administrative expenses.

Responsibilities

Regional Business Partnering

Serve as the single finance point of contact for the Regional Presidents, with a dotted line into the Regional President and a seat on the regional leadership team
Lead the teams to deliver integrated commercial support and finance business partnering
Partner with Country Managing Directors, Corporate Development, and Business Development on regional priorities and trade-offs
Provide clear, concise, commercially focused communication on how the business achieves its financial, strategic, and operational outcomes

Metro and Regional Strategy

Align on metro strategy with Regional Presidents, Country Managing Directors, and other regional leaders, pushing for improved long-term financial outcomes
Support new market funding and acceleration decisions with rigorous business cases and clear return expectations
Hold the line on long-term financial outcomes while execution stays owned within each respective function

Asset Management and Commercial Value Levers

Provide critical strategic and operational expertise and judgment in the commercial decision-making process to achieve return on invested capital aspirations
Improve financial outcomes across pricing, revenue opportunities, delivery timing, volume, ecosystem, capacity, operational scale, and regulatory levers
Partner with Sales, Global Territory Management Operations, Capacity, Operations, and Corporate Development to understand commercial drivers and maximize return on invested capital
Drive value through local, regional, and global initiatives, from new market acceleration to pricing strategy

Profit and Loss Visibility and Insight

Collaborate with Customer and Revenue Finance, Operations Finance, xScale Finance, and other teams to build a complete view of country and regional performance
Provide profit and loss visibility, insight on business performance, and advice to local leaders on opportunities and risks
Coordinate forecasting, budgeting, and reporting of Regional President selling, general, and administrative expenses
Support delivery of business-case returns across the regional investment portfolio

Transactions and Corporate Development

Partner with the Regional President and Regional Corporate Development leader on mergers and acquisitions and other large transactions
Coordinate with the Global Mergers and Acquisitions Finance team on valuation, diligence, and approvals
Support in-region integration and post-close performance tracking against the business case

Team Leadership and Culture

Lead a regionally distributed team
Build a diverse, high-performing team that makes a positive impact on culture
Align to enterprise standards, systems, and calendars set by Corporate Financial Planning and Analysis and the Financial Planning and Analysis Center of Excellence

Qualifications

Required Experience

Proven years in a commercial or finance role responsible for understanding and driving financial outcomes
Proven experience leading and managing regional finance teams of more than ten people
Commercial and financial leadership in the data center industry, or similar real estate or technology industries
Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, or a related field
Strong analytical, problem-solving, and organizational skills

Preferred Experience

Master's degree (MBA) or equivalent advanced business credential
Experience partnering with regional presidents, country leaders, and other executive stakeholders
Exposure to mergers and acquisitions and other large transactions in coordination with a global deal team
Track record of developing long-term strategies that align with organizational goals
Success in a fast-paced, dynamic environment managing multiple priorities

Competencies

Commercial acumen and financial rigor
Trusted advisor to senior leadership
Influence across functions and geographies
Risk mitigation and long-term profitability
Detail depth with big-picture storytelling
Collaborative, results-oriented mindset
Distributed team leadership

jobs.title: Director, Financial Reporting & Internal Controls
jobs.description:
At Mitel, you will have the opportunity to help businesses connect, collaborate and provide better experiences for our customers. You will deliver valuable contributions in creating business success within our global organization utilizing your unique attributes, skills and experience.

Please take a moment to look over this opportunity and if interested, feel free to send us your application. If this is not the right opportunity for you, you can also sign up for Job Alerts by creating an account. This will give you a profile that you can use for all future applications, and you will be notified whenever a new position that matches your criteria becomes available.

The Director, Financial Reporting & Internal Controls is responsible for the Company’s consolidated financial reporting, technical accounting, global statutory reporting and audit activities, and oversight of the internal control environment. This role will oversee a small team, providing day-to-day leadership, coaching, workload prioritization and performance support while ensuring high-quality execution of key reporting and control deliverables. The role partners closely with senior finance leadership, regional finance teams, cross-functional stakeholders and external auditors.

Key Responsibilities

Prepare the Company’s quarterly and annual consolidated financial statements and related disclosures in accordance with IFRS.
Support quarterly and annual reporting processes and review significant accounting entries and adjustments.
Ensure consistency and accuracy of financial reporting across the organization.
Lead the consolidated financial statement audit, acting as the primary relationship manager with external auditors, coordinating key deliverables, reviewing and participating in the negotiation of audit fees, and resolving audit and accounting matters.
Serve as a key technical accounting resource and lead the assessment and documentation of complex and non-routine transactions under IFRS, including revenue recognition, share-based compensation, leases, pensions, restructuring and provisions, impairments, business combinations, legal entity restructuring and other complex accounting matters.
Monitor new accounting standards and developments and assess their impact on the Company’s financial reporting and accounting policies.
Oversee global statutory financial statements, audits and required filings across multiple jurisdictions, including managing the statutory audit calendar, coordinating with local finance teams, external auditors and service providers, monitoring progress and driving timely completion.
Oversee the financial internal control environment, including monitoring key controls, identifying control gaps and supporting remediation activities.
Partner with Tax, Treasury, Legal and other functions on significant transactions, restructurings and other accounting matters.
Support acquisitions, integrations, legal entity restructurings and other strategic initiatives from an accounting and financial reporting perspective.
Drive continuous improvement and standardization of financial reporting, statutory audit and related finance processes.
Lead, coach and develop a small team, including setting priorities, assigning work, providing timely feedback and supporting professional growth.
Promote a collaborative, high-performance team environment with clear expectations, effective communication and accountability for deliverables.
Support ad hoc projects and transactions as required.

Requirements

Must hold a recognized professional accounting designation (CPA, ACA, or ACCA).
10+ years of progressive accounting and financial reporting experience, preferably including experience in a large multinational organization and/or public accounting.
Strong knowledge of IFRS.
Experience in preparing consolidated financial statements and related disclosures.
Strong technical accounting research and documentation skills.
Experience managing external audits and global statutory reporting requirements.
Experience working across multiple legal entities, jurisdictions and finance teams.
Strong project management skills with demonstrated ability to manage multiple concurrent deadlines.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills and ability to communicate complex accounting matters clearly to both finance and non-finance stakeholders.
Demonstrated people management experience, including coaching, developing and managing the performance of direct reports in a finance or accounting environment.
Experience with SAP, BlackLine and financial consolidation/reporting systems is an asset.

Vacancy: Replacement

Salary Range: $130,000- $150,000

Job Description:

Associate Director, Investment Management Data – SLC Management

What is in it for you:

Reporting to the Director, Investments Data Product, this role will be part of a dedicated Agile team and will be accountable for delivering investment data products through a highly dynamic and fast-paced solution development process.

The Associate Director will work closely with business stakeholders, data engineers, architects, and development teams to transform business concepts and data requirements into scalable solutions. This role is accountable for balancing business priorities, user needs, data quality requirements, governance objectives, and technology considerations while ensuring successful business outcomes.

The Associate Director will combine product ownership responsibilities with hands-on data analysis and domain expertise to define, develop, and continuously improve investment data products used across the organization.

What You Will Do

Contribute to the strategy, roadmap, and ongoing evolution of investment data products by translating business priorities into scalable solutions that improve decision-making, analytics, operational efficiency, and information management.
Partner with business and technology stakeholders to understand business processes, challenges, and data requirements, translating needs into user stories, acceptance criteria, data mappings, process documentation, and solution designs.
Perform data analysis, profiling, reconciliation, validation, and root-cause investigations across investment and accounting data domains, while collaborating with engineers and architects to design scalable data models, transformation rules, and reusable data products.
Own and prioritize the product backlog, ensuring delivery teams have clear requirements, priorities, and expected outcomes, while actively supporting Agile ceremonies, testing, user acceptance activities, and release readiness.
Support enterprise data governance, quality, and control initiatives by establishing and monitoring data standards, testing practices, lineage, metadata, and business glossary requirements.
Build strong relationships with stakeholders by communicating product priorities, roadmaps, progress, risks, and outcomes, while supporting change management and user adoption activities.
Contribute to the definition, tracking, and achievement of product and initiative objectives and key results (OKRs), measuring success through adoption, data quality, operational efficiency, and business outcomes.

What You Need To Succeed

6+ years of experience in Asset Management, Capital Markets, Investment Operations, Investment Technology, or a related field, with a strong understanding of investment products, portfolios, transactions, performance, benchmarks, market data, reference data, and investment lifecycle processes.
Demonstrated experience partnering with business stakeholders in data-intensive environments, including business analysis, requirements gathering, process improvement, data profiling, data mapping, testing, and solution delivery.
Strong knowledge of enterprise data management concepts, including data governance, data quality, data modeling, architecture, system integration, investment data platforms, and complex datasets, supported by advanced SQL and analytical skills.
Experience working as a Product Owner, Business Analyst, Data Analyst, or similar role within Agile delivery environments, with responsibility for backlog management, prioritization, user story development, and iterative solution delivery.
Proven ability to independently solve complex business and technology challenges, manage competing priorities, navigate ambiguity, influence stakeholders, and translate business needs into actionable solutions and measurable outcomes.
Experience with investment systems and enterprise data platforms is considered an asset.

Why SLC Management?

Opportunity to work for a growing global institutional asset manager
Excellent benefits and wellness programs to support the three pillars of your well-being – mental, physical and financial – including generous vacation and sick time, market-leading maternity, parental and adoption leave top up program, a partially-paid sabbatical program and much more
Pension, stock and savings programs with an employer-paid match to help build and enhance your future financial security
A flexible work environment with a friendly, caring, collaborative and inclusive culture focused on career growth development #WeWinAsATeam
The opportunity to move along a variety of career paths with amazing networking potential
Award winning workplace culture - Great Place to Work® Certified in Canada and the U.S., “Best Places to Work” by Glassdoor, Award for Excellence for Mental Health at Work, “Best Places to Work in Money Management” by Pension & Investments
